trở đi, từ đó về sau
From next Monday onwards, the store will open an hour earlier.
little: There is little time left before the deadline arrives.
until: up to the point in time that something happens
It worked until it did not.
her: belonging to a female previously mentioned
She left her umbrella on the train this morning.
catches: reaches the same level as something after being behind
Production finally catches up with demand after months of shortage.
back: returning to a previous place, position or condition
She promised to call him back as soon as she landed.
lost: no longer possessed, or unable to find one's way
The hikers got lost on the mountain trail at dusk.
during: throughout the course of a period of time
She stayed awake during the entire overnight bus journey.
gap: a difference or space between two things
The gap between rich and poor neighbourhoods keeps growing.
reason: a cause or explanation for something
Nobody knew the real reason for his sudden resignation.
worse: Trying to write the same content from memory feels far worse — and works far better.
official: approved by a person or group in authority; formal
The government made an official announcement about the new policy.
figures: numbers or diagrams used to present information
The report included figures showing sales over the past decade.
suggest: to put forward an idea or possibility
The data suggest that sales will rise again next quarter.
fight: to struggle against something using force or effort
Doctors are working hard to fight the spread of the disease.
high: extending a long way upward; great in degree
The wall around the property is unusually high.
central: relating to the most important or main part of something
The central government approved new funding for rural schools.
banks: financial institutions that keep and lend money
Most banks now offer free online transfers for customers.
rates: speeds at which things happen, or fixed prices or measures
Interest rates rose sharply after the central bank's announcement.
borrowing: the act of taking and using something that belongs to someone else, promising to return it
Borrowing tools from the neighbours saved them a lot of money.
spending: the act of using money or time on something
The government announced cuts to public spending this year.
slows: Heavy rain always slows the traffic on this road.
calm: to become quieter, less intense, or less agitated
Traders hope the market will calm down after this week's volatility.
down: toward a lower position or level
Please sit down and make yourself comfortable.
cost: the amount of money needed to buy, do, or produce something
The cost of the renovation was far higher than the family expected.
slower: moving or happening at a reduced speed, compared with something else
The old computer is much slower than the new one.
growth: the process of increasing, or a layer that has developed
Algal growth on the pond's surface blocked most of the sunlight.
jobs: paid positions of employment or tasks
New factories created thousands of jobs in the region.
zero: Yet most economists do not want zero inflation either.
either: used to refer to one or the other of two options
You can choose either the red one or the blue one.
small: not large in size, amount, or degree
They live in a small apartment near the city center.
steady: not changing, moving or shaking; firm and regular
He kept a steady pace throughout the marathon.
generally: People generally prefer shorter commutes to work.
seen: The old photographs had not been seen for decades.
healthy: in good physical or mental condition
A healthy diet includes plenty of fruit and vegetables.
falling: She watched the falling leaves drift across the yard.
lead: to go in front of, guide, or result in something
Good habits often lead to better health over time.
delay: a period of time when something happens later than planned
The flight was cancelled after a long delay at the gate.
weaken: to make or become less strong
Falling prices can lead people to delay spending and weaken the economy.
think: to use the mind to consider something or form an opinion
I need some time to think before I answer you.
again: She read the letter again before deciding what to write back.
about: The lecture was about how cities cope with extreme heat.
notes: short written records made to help someone remember something
She reviewed her notes carefully before the final exam.
did: past tense of 'do', used to form questions and negatives or as a main verb
She did all her homework before watching television last night.
world: the earth and all its people and things
The trouble starts when the body's clock and the world's clock disagree.
around: The children ran around the playground chasing each other happily.
banknote: He found an old banknote hidden inside a book.
really: I really enjoyed the concert despite the terrible weather.
promise: to give an assurance that something will happen
The new treatment seems to promise real relief for chronic pain sufferers.
exchanged: given and received in return for something else
No metal had ever been exchanged to create the original debt.
weakens: Left alone, the starter runs out of flour and weakens over time.
gently: in a mild, careful, or soft manner
một cách nhẹ nhàng, từ từ
He gently placed the sleeping baby into the crib.
predictably: in a way that can be expected in advance
một cách có thể đoán trước
Traffic predictably slows to a crawl every weekday at five o'clock.
plan: a detailed scheme for achieving something
They drew up a plan to renovate the old library.
trust: firm belief in the reliability or honesty of someone or something
The conditions that make local management work include a group small enough to know one another and trust each other.
begins: The film begins with a dramatic scene in the mountains.
break: to separate into pieces, or stop working, suddenly
Cheap umbrellas often break after just one windy day.
far: to a great extent; at or to a great distance
This plan works far better than the last one did.
harder: more difficult or more solid; comparative of hard
The second exam was noticeably harder than the first.
rebuild: to build something again after it has been damaged or destroyed
It took years to rebuild the town after the devastating earthquake.
any: used to refer to one or some of a thing, no matter which
Do you have any questions before we begin the meeting?
